summary: The finite-set witness lemma is proved without closedness or affine-rank assumptions on the original convex sets. The compact threshold maximization produces distinct exposed vertices and excludes every other point of the finite set from their convex hull. The graph midpoint condition and parity pigeonhole argument consequently bound every empty vertex set by 2^n. The atomic selection argument uses this exact graph as its location set and the stated normalized weights, and proves a single point with the required depth in the positive-support convex hull. Singleton sets, zero total weight, zero individual weights, lower affine ranks, strict heavy-halfspace thresholds, and closed-halfspace boundary atoms cause no exception. The declared alias map matches the generic construction in the accepted predecessor; no product-location-set conclusion is imported into the graph theorem. No mathematical error or proof gap was found.
